_comment: Golden table for the NativePathSet workspace root set rules, read by both
The cross-field rules necessarily exist twice, once as the Zod refinement in
shared/contracts/src/native-path-contract.ts and once as the hand-authored Python
module sandbox_manager.native_isolation.path_set_rules. This table is what keeps them
identical: each case is applied as a shallow override of `base`, and both suites
assert that the set of refusal reason codes equals `expected_reasons` exactly.
`expected_reasons` is compared as a sorted set, so ordering is not part of the
contract but membership is. An empty list means the descriptor must be accepted.
Reason codes are the closed enumeration in native-path-contract.ts, generated into
Several cases legitimately produce more than one code. Where that happens the note
says why, because it is a property of the rules rather than test noise.

cases.name: installer_provisioned_only_is_accepted
cases.note: A user who adds nothing gets a one-member set describing today's layout.

cases.name: a_wrong_contract_version_is_shape_fatal
cases.note: No cross-field rule explains a wrong version, and Zod 4 skips object refinements after an invalid_value issue, so both languages must report the safety-net code rather than an empty refusal.

cases.name: an_unknown_descriptor_field_is_shape_fatal
cases.note: Both shape layers forbid extra keys, and Zod 4 skips object refinements after an unrecognized_keys issue. Same safety-net code, for the same reason as a wrong version.

cases.name: second_root_is_a_new_member_not_a_new_field
cases.note: Adding a root adds an array member. No descriptor field and no schema changes.

cases.name: read_only_grant_is_accepted
cases.note: user_granted_ro with a read_only access mode is consistent.

cases.name: extended_prefix_member_spelling_is_refused
cases.note: A legal spelling is not a canonical one. The extended prefix names the same directory and folds to the same id, which is exactly the problem: the member would say \\?\D:\Work while every rule reasoned about D:\Work. It is refused, not rewritten.

cases.name: lowercase_drive_letter_member_spelling_is_refused
cases.note: The other legal-but-not-canonical spelling. Same directory, same id, refused for the same reason.

cases.name: member_count_at_bound_is_accepted
cases.note: The declared maximum is inclusive.

cases.name: two_members_overlap_each_other
cases.note: Category 1. One pairwise rule covers member against member.

cases.name: member_under_a_fixed_managed_root
cases.note: Category 2. The member lives inside payload_root.

cases.name: member_is_the_payload_root
cases.note: Category 10. Equality with a fixed managed root, same generalized rule.

cases.name: two_fixed_managed_roots_overlap
cases.note: The same pairwise rule still covers fixed root against fixed root.

cases.name: non_canonical_dot_dot_traversal
cases.note: Category 3. Derivation is not attempted for a path that has no canonical form.

cases.name: non_canonical_trailing_dot
cases.note: Category 3.

cases.name: non_canonical_trailing_space
cases.note: Category 3.

cases.name: non_canonical_forward_slashes
cases.note: Category 3.

cases.name: relative_path
cases.note: Category 4.

cases.name: volume_root_plain
cases.note: Category 5. A whole volume gets its own reason code.

cases.name: volume_root_extended_prefix
cases.note: Category 5.

cases.name: member_is_the_owner_profile_root
cases.note: Category 6. The host supplies the profile path; the contract never reads USERPROFILE. The profile also contains %LOCALAPPDATA%, and containment is tested in both directions, so that rule fires too.

cases.name: member_under_local_app_data
cases.note: Category 7.

cases.name: member_under_program_data
cases.note: Category 8. Also overlaps protected_root and isolation_root, which live there, so the disjointness rule fires too.

cases.name: member_under_the_windows_directory
cases.note: Category 9.

cases.name: member_under_another_users_profile
cases.note: Category 11. Under the users container but not under the owner's own profile.

cases.name: volume_verdict_non_ntfs
cases.note: Category 12. The verdict is a caller-supplied input, never measured here.

cases.name: volume_verdict_removable
cases.note: Category 13.

cases.name: volume_verdict_redirected
cases.note: Category 14.

cases.name: volume_verdict_unknown_fails_closed
cases.note: Category 15. Absent evidence is refused rather than defaulted to a pass.

cases.name: ancestor_reparse_point_observed
cases.note: Category 16. A point-in-time lstat observation, not a race-aware check.

cases.name: ancestry_verdict_unknown_fails_closed
cases.note: Category 16 companion. A walk that could not complete is refused.

cases.name: member_count_above_bound
cases.note: Category 17. Nine members against a declared maximum of eight.

cases.name: member_count_below_bound
cases.note: An empty set breaks the lower bound and has no managed_default, so both fire.

cases.name: zero_managed_default_members
cases.note: Category 18.

cases.name: two_managed_default_members
cases.note: Category 19.

cases.name: access_mode_inconsistent_with_policy_class
cases.note: Category 20. user_granted_ro must be read_only.

cases.name: user_grant_without_a_grant_record
cases.note: A user-granted root carrying the installer-provisioned record is inconsistent.

cases.name: managed_default_carrying_a_user_grant
cases.note: The installer-provisioned root must not claim a user grant.

cases.name: duplicate_root_id
cases.note: Category 21. The repeated id cannot also be the derivation of the second path.

cases.name: duplicate_canonical_path
cases.note: Category 22. Identical paths also share a derived id and trivially overlap.

cases.name: duplicate_canonical_path_by_case_alias
cases.note: Comparison is case-insensitive, so a case alias is the same canonical path. The alias differs in a component, not in the drive letter, because a lowercase drive letter is refused as a non-canonical spelling before this rule is reached.

cases.name: root_id_not_derived_from_path
cases.note: The id is host-derived, so a supplied id that does not match its path is refused.

cases.name: member_contains_the_local_app_data_root
cases.note: Containing a denied location grants everything inside it, so the rule tests containment in both directions. The default layout hid this because the fixed backend roots sit under %LOCALAPPDATA%; here they are on another volume, as a relocated state directory puts them.

cases.name: member_contains_a_users_container_root
cases.note: A relocated profile container one level deeper, so the containing member is not a volume root. The member holds the relocated profiles, and with them the owner's %LOCALAPPDATA%, so both rules fire. It is the first of the two containers that matches; one refusal is emitted however many match.

cases.name: member_in_the_system_users_directory_while_the_profile_is_relocated
cases.note: The owner's profile lives on another volume, so the parent of %USERPROFILE% is not C:\Users - but C:\Users still holds Default, Public, and every account that was not relocated. A single-valued container field could only name one of the two and naming the relocated one reopened this member.

cases.name: short_name_alias_spelling_of_a_denied_ancestor
cases.note: C:\PROGRA~3 is the live 8.3 alias of C:\ProgramData. Accepting it would leave the denied-location rule comparing against a spelling nothing else uses.

cases.name: short_name_alias_spelling_of_one_users_container_root
cases.note: Every entry of the container list is checked, not just the first. An alias spelling in the second entry would compare against a spelling nothing else uses, so the whole list would silently stop matching the directory it names.

cases.name: short_name_alias_spelling_of_a_fixed_managed_root
cases.note: The alias spelling of a fixed root would compare as a different directory from every other root, so disjointness would pass on two names for one place.

cases.name: short_name_alias_member_under_a_denied_ancestor
cases.note: The long spelling of this member refuses with member_overlaps_managed_root and member_under_program_data_root. The alias spelling must not be the way around them.

cases.name: short_name_alias_member_aliasing_another_member
cases.note: Read-only on the long spelling and read-write on the alias would be two members naming one directory, with the stricter access mode simply bypassed.

cases.name: short_name_alias_member_with_no_retained_base
cases.note: Once nothing of the long name survives generation the alias is bare, as in ~1. An earlier pattern required at least one character before the tilde and accepted this spelling.

cases.name: a_shape_fatal_version_hides_a_second_managed_default
cases.note: A shape-fatal failure wins outright in both languages: the version is not one this contract can parse, so no verdict about field semantics is reported alongside it. Without this case the two tiers could disagree here and every other case would still pass.

cases.name: an_unknown_field_hides_a_duplicated_member
cases.note: Same rule, reached by an unknown key rather than a wrong literal. The duplicated member would refuse on its own id and on its own path, and neither code is reported.

cases.name: an_unreadable_vocabulary_hides_an_overlap_with_a_managed_root
cases.note: A verdict outside its closed vocabulary is unreadable rather than merely wrong, so the member it describes states no fact this contract can weigh. The second member is isolation_root and sits under program_data_root, and neither code is reported.

cases.name: a_field_of_the_wrong_type_hides_a_duplicated_member
cases.note: A number where a path belongs is not a spelling this contract can evaluate, so the same rule applies as for a wrong version. A fourth route to the verdict, because each of these is a different Zod issue kind and a different Pydantic error type.

cases.name: a_member_path_failing_the_grammar_is_not_shape_fatal
cases.note: The other side of the same line, and why it is drawn at parseability rather than at any failure at all. A path with forward slashes is a well-typed string whose content is wrong: it carries its own code, and the cross-field rules still run and still report the duplicated id.
